name: WHO-5 Well-Being Index
developer: WHO Regional Office for Europe, Psychiatric Research Unit, Hillerød (Bech) (1998)
construct: Subjective psychological wellbeing (positive mood, vitality and interest) over the past 2 weeks.
licence: CORC: "The WHO-5 is free of charge and does not require permission to use." PsyToolkit 'Legal stuff': the WHO-5 can be used for research provided the authors and their research paper are acknowledged.
instructions: Please respond to each item regarding how you felt in the last two weeks.

items.text: Over the past two weeks ... I have felt cheerful in good spirits.
items.note: PsyToolkit omits 'and'; the WHO original and Te Pou read 'I have felt cheerful and in good spirits.'

items.text: Over the past two weeks ... I have felt calm and relaxed.
Over the past two weeks ... I have felt active and vigorous.
Over the past two weeks ... I woke up feeling fresh and rested.
Over the past two weeks ... My daily life has been filled with things that interest me.

scoring: Sum the 5 items (0 to 25) and multiply by 4 to give a percentage score from 0 (worst) to 100 (best). Higher scores indicate better wellbeing. Topp et al. (2015): a score below 51 (that is, 50 or lower) is commonly used as a screening cut off for depression and warrants further assessment; a change of 10 percentage points is considered clinically relevant. Some studies use a lower cut off depending on the population.
citation: World Health Organization Regional Office for Europe. (1998). Wellbeing measures in primary health care/The DepCare Project: Report on a WHO meeting, Stockholm, Sweden, 12–13 February 1998. WHO Regional Office for Europe. See also Topp, C. W., Østergaard, S. D., Søndergaard, S., & Bech, P. (2015). The WHO-5 Well-Being Index: A systematic review of the literature. Psychotherapy and Psychosomatics, 84(3), 167–176. https://doi.org/10.1159/000376585
transcriptionNote: Items, stem, instruction and response values transcribed from the PsyToolkit survey library page. Item 1 on PsyToolkit reads 'cheerful in good spirits' whereas the WHO original (quoted on tepou.co.nz) reads 'cheerful and in good spirits'; PsyToolkit wording retained verbatim with the difference flagged. CORC prints the response labels as 'More than half of the time' and 'Less than half of the time'; PsyToolkit omits 'of'. The official WHO form (psykiatri-regionh.dk) was not fetched, so its instruction wording was not compared.
